note: Willie L. Brown Jr. Institute fact base — extracted from the Education OS app by tools/extract_fact_bases.py and canonical here since v0.39.0. The disclaimer travels verbatim with every use; principles carry their source attribution.
org: The Willie L. Brown Jr. Institute of Politics and Public Service (wlbinstitute.org), San Francisco
disclaimer: This track is a proposal built from the Institute's public mission and the Willie L. Brown Jr. Fellowship Program at San Francisco State University. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or reviewed by the Institute, SF State, or Mayor Brown; the "Willie Brown Foundation" name in the brief refers to this Institute. A named track would be offered under a partnership agreement and the Institute's review of every course.
mission: The Institute provides education and training for emerging leaders while fostering civic engagement, leadership development and effective governance, with an emphasis on inclusivity and diversity — preparing next-generation leaders to address complex societal challenges.
quote: Public service is the most noble of professions. It provides the opportunity to give back to your community, to ensure the next generation has opportunities to lead better lives.
record: Four decades in California public life
Assembly Speaker and two-term Mayor of San Francisco; worked across administrations from Pat Brown to Arnold Schwarzenegger
Revitalized public transit as mayor — the civic machine every child rides
Advanced affordable housing through bond measures — money, votes and buildings
Reformed juvenile justice — second chances as public policy
Developed UCSF's Mission Bay campus as a biotech hub — science, jobs and a neighborhood
Civil rights, education reform, tax policy, economic development, healthcare, affirmative action

principles.p: Public service is the most noble of professions
principles.teach: Service is taught as a craft with roles, crews, evidence and credentials — not as a slogan. Every course ends with a real audience.

principles.p: Recruit and include students of diverse racial, cultural and economic backgrounds
principles.src: Willie L. Brown Jr., on the Fellowship (SF State News)
principles.teach: Who is in the room is a design decision. Every course asks who is missing and why; accommodation profiles, four-language signals and Tier 0 parity apply; barriers are named, not hidden.

principles.p: Hands-on learning inside real public agencies, with a cohort, a seminar and a stipend
principles.src: The Fellowship Program (SF State ICCE): 16 hours a week, 15 weeks, Friday seminars, cohort focused on equity and social change
principles.teach: A junior placement at every grade band and a weekly seminar circle from grade 3; in 11–12 a supervised, FLSA-compliant placement mirrors the Fellowship itself.

principles.p: Share knowledge and skills with a new generation of leaders
principles.src: Institute mission; Claremont McKenna Athenaeum description of Brown's mentoring role
principles.teach: Mentorship is a strand and a bridge: alumni and public servants as mentors and panelists; older students mentor younger cohorts; the leader's-story module in every course.

principles.p: Eagerly, aggressively and affirmatively push for those who have been blocked by the ceiling
principles.src: Willie L. Brown Jr., NPR interview on Basic Brown (2008)
principles.teach: Affirmative action, first-generation pathways and opportunity data are taught as history, law and practice — with the debate included, not avoided.

principles.p: Take on the cases others dismiss as hopeless
principles.src: Brown's early law career (Claremont McKenna Athenaeum)
principles.teach: Civil-rights law, housing discrimination (the 1960 sit-in), the Free Speech Movement defense: courses on standing up when the odds are long, with moot courts and rights cases to argue.

principles.p: Tolerate diverse viewpoints; some opposing ideas strengthen consensus
principles.src: NPR summary of Basic Brown's political lessons
principles.teach: Negotiation, coalition and consensus are practiced every week in the seminar circle and in mock legislatures; the fifteen-year Speakership is the case study.

principles.p: What you see is what you get — transparency removes the liability and lets you move on to substance
principles.teach: Ethics, transparency and accountability strand: public records, conflicts of interest, the investigator's question, saying the hard thing first.

principles.src: Larry Berry, Fellowship alumnus (SF State PACE alumni spotlight)
principles.teach: Inclusive decision-making and relationship-building are taught as skills with evidence: stakeholder maps, crew hand-offs, the "who did we forget" check before every presentation.

principles.p: Decisions in the public sector must account for the wide-ranging impacts on people's lives
principles.teach: Every policy-design course carries an impact analysis: who pays, who benefits, who is displaced — in real numbers from the state's own data.

principles.p: From segregated Mineola to San Francisco State: education as the bridge across barriers
principles.src: Biography (HistoryMakers; African American Registry): born 1934, Mineola, Texas; moved to San Francisco in 1951; SF State 1955; Hastings 1958
principles.teach: The first-generation strand and the Mineola-to-City bridge: oral histories, the story of one's own family's barrier-crossing, and the concrete map from a K–12 credential to a state university and a public-service career.

principles.p: Living large: enjoy the work and share the joy
principles.src: Willie L. Brown Jr., NPR interview
principles.teach: Presence, confidence and joy in service are taught age-appropriately — public speaking, presentation, the civic celebration — because a leader who dreads the room cannot bring anyone along.
